title: Secret Tapes: Did Joe Biden Share Classified Info and Forget Things?
summary: Imagine finding old recordings of a former vice president talking about top-secret things—and sometimes forgetting what he was saying. That's exactly what just happened with Joe Biden! A group called the Oversight Project released about three hours of audio tapes from 2016 and 2017. In them, Biden chats with Mark Zwonitzer, the writer helping him with his memoir (a book about his life). At the time, Biden had just finished being vice president under Barack Obama. On the tapes, Biden seems to share classified information—details the government keeps secret to protect the country. In one recording, he says, "I just found all the classified stuff downstairs." He also talks about a secret 40-page memo he wrote to President Obama arguing against sending more troops to Afghanistan. The really sensitive parts are bleeped out, so we can't hear them. But here's the twist: Biden also struggles to remember some dates and facts. In one part, he can't recall when certain events happened. This became a big deal because in 2024, a special lawyer named Robert Hur investigated Biden for how he handled classified papers. Hur decided not to charge Biden, but said a jury might see him as a "sympathetic" older man with a "poor memory." That comment caused a huge argument about whether Biden was too old to be president. Biden's team says the tapes were private and should never have been released. They call it a political attack. The Oversight Project says the public has a right to know. A court agreed, and now we're all listening in on a piece of history.
why_it_matters: If a leader shares secrets or cannot remember important things, people might not trust them to make safe decisions, just like you would want a dependable partner for a big class project.

background_read: When leaders leave office they are supposed to return all secret papers to the government because keeping them can be dangerous.
Other former top officials, like Donald Trump, have also been investigated for holding onto classified documents after leaving office.
Memoirs by former presidents and vice presidents often talk about big events, but they are not allowed to reveal national secrets.
Article_Structure: WHO: Former Vice President Joe Biden and the writer Mark Zwonitzer
WHAT: Three hours of old audio recordings were released, showing Biden seeming to share classified information and struggling to remember things.
WHERE: The recordings were from 2016 and 2017, after Biden had finished being vice president.
WHY: The Oversight Project wanted the public to hear them; Biden's team says it is a political attack, and the memory issue renewed questions about his age.

perspectives.description: They say these were private conversations taken out of context and that forgetting small details doesn't mean someone can't lead.
They argue that the public deserves to know if a president mishandled secrets and whether his memory might affect his judgment.
They are split—some think the taped remarks could be a crime, while others note that no charges were filed because the evidence was weak.
